Issues.Title: fix(forms): support nullable and optional string in email and pattern validators
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`email()` and `pattern()` signal form validators only accept `SchemaPath<string, ...>` paths. This causes TypeScript compilation errors when fields are represented as nullable or optional types (e.g., `string | null` or `string | null | undefined`), even though at runtime `isEmpty()` already treats `null` and `undefined` as empty values that pass validation.

Issue Number: #66539

## What is the new behavior?

Relaxes the generic constraint on `email()` and `pattern()` to `TValue extends string | null | undefined`.
Now fields typed as `string | null`, `string | undefined`, or `string | null | undefined` can be validated without type errors.

Supersedes #68855.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): report errors at arrow parameters
Issues.Body:
Fixes #71733

## Why the change

Under `strictTemplates`, a TypeScript error that starts at a template arrow function parameter, such as a callback that declares a parameter its caller never passes, is silently dropped; with this fix Angular reports it at the parameter.

## Special things to note

- This PR rewrites the existing spec `should ignore diagnostics on arrow function parameters`, which asserted the `D:ignore` marker. The marker's only purpose was hiding implicit `any` errors, and those stay hidden. See [Why the old `D:ignore` spec changes](#why-the-old-dignore-spec-changes).
- The fix depends on correct parameter locations. The parser left the expression's offset out of them, so inside `{{…}}` they started too early (`{(val` instead of `val`, and further off in later interpolations). This PR fixes that too. Event bindings have no offset, so they weren't affected.
- Newly reported errors also include duplicate parameter names: `(a, a) => a` now reports TS2300 at both `a`s. Language service: go-to-definition on an arrow parameter reference now returns the parameter (`val`) instead of the enclosing expression (`val + 1`).

## Change outline

The template from the issue:

```html
<button (click)="retry((attempt) => load(attempt))">Retry</button>
```

What the type-check block emits for the arrow function. Other location comments are left out:

```diff
- (this).retry(attempt /*D:ignore*/ => ...)
+ (this).retry(attempt /*24,31*/ => ...)
```

How the TS2345 error, which starts at `attempt`, is mapped back to the template:

```diff
 translateDiagnostic(TS2345 at `attempt`)
   shouldReportDiagnostic            → TS2345 isn't filtered by code
   findSourceLocation(`attempt`)
-    has the D:ignore marker         → null → error dropped
+    has a location comment          → reported at `attempt`
```

Parameter locations from the parser, for `{{a}} {{(foo, bar) => foo + bar}}`:

```diff
- foo → `{a}} {{(foo`    bar → `{{(foo, bar`
+ foo → `foo`            bar → `bar`
```

### Why the old `D:ignore` spec changes

`type_check_block_spec.ts` had `should ignore diagnostics on arrow function parameters`, which expected `(a /*D:ignore*/, b /*D:ignore*/) =>`. It came from 87a422358b (#66294), the commit that added template arrow functions. The commit message and the PR don't discuss the marker. The one stated reason is the code comment that commit put on it:

> Ignore diagnostics on the node to skip diagnostics from `noImplicitAny` since users aren't able to set types on the parameters. Note that this is preferable to setting their types to `any`, because it allows us to infer the types when the arrow function is passed as a callback.

Both goals still hold without the marker:

| What the marker protected | What protects it now | Spec, all passing before and after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No implicit `any` error (TS7006) on parameters that templates can't annotate | `shouldReportDiagnostic` drops TS7006 everywhere in the type-check block. It has done so since 2019 (#33125), before arrow functions existed. Template arrow parameters can only be plain names, so TS7006 is the only implicit `any` error they can produce. | `should not report implicit any errors on arrow functions defined in @let` (existing, from the same commit, unchanged), `should not report implicit any errors on arrow functions without a contextual type` (new) |
| Parameter types are still inferred from the callback, not forced to `any` | Unchanged. Parameters are still emitted without a type; only the trailing comment differs. | `should infer the types of parameters of arrow functions passed in as callbacks` (existing, unchanged), `should not report errors on contextually typed arrow function parameters` (new) |
| (Not stated, but also hidden) Unused parameter errors (TS6133, TS6199) | `shouldReportDiagnostic` drops both codes. | `should not report unused arrow function parameters` (new, in `typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts`, with `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`) |

The marker also hid every other error that starts at a parameter, which is the bug this PR fixes. The rewritten spec, `should add span info to arrow function parameters`, now expects `(a /*3,4*/, b /*6,7*/) =>`.

Changed files:

```text
packages/compiler/src/
├── typecheck/expression.ts           # parameter gets a location comment, not D:ignore
└── expression_parser/parser.ts       # parameter location includes the expression offset
packages/compiler-cli/
├── test/ngtsc/template_typecheck_spec.ts               # 2 specs that fail before, 2 that must stay silent
├── src/ngtsc/typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts        # duplicate names (fails before), unused parameters (stays silent)
└── src/ngtsc/typecheck/test/type_check_block_spec.ts   # expects location comments
packages/compiler/test/expression_parser/parser_spec.ts # parameter locations in a second {{…}}
packages/language-service/test/definitions_spec.ts      # expects `val` instead of `val + 1`
```

## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

A template type error is not reported when TypeScript places it at an arrow function parameter. Examples are a callback with more parameters than its caller passes, a callback that returns a function instead of a value, and duplicate parameter names.

Issue Number: #71733

## What is the new behavior?

The error is reported at the parameter. Implicit `any` and unused-parameter errors on template arrow functions are still not reported.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Apps that contain such an error will now fail to compile under `strictTemplates`. The error was always there, but Angular didn't report it.

## Other information

The duplicate-name and unused-parameter specs are in `typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts` rather than the ngtsc suite. Under the preprocessor backend (`ngtsc_ngp`), the compiled component code is type-checked as well, and its copy of the arrow function produces its own `Duplicate identifier` and TS6133 errors without a template location. That happens with and without this PR. `diagnostics_spec.ts` checks only the type-check block, so these specs pass on both backends.

Template arrow functions were added in 21.2.0, so 22.2.x has this bug too. This is a candidate for the patch branch. #52322 is a precedent: it surfaced comparison errors that an ignore marker hid, landed as a plain fix, and was cherry-picked to the release branch.

Issues.Title: Template type checking drops errors that start at an arrow function parameter
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler, compiler-cli

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `strictTemplates`, Angular doesn't report a type error in a template arrow function when TypeScript places that error at one of the function's parameters. The template compiles, and the mistake reaches runtime.

A common case is a callback that declares a parameter the caller never passes:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  template: `<button (click)="retry((attempt) => load(attempt))">Retry</button>`,
})
export class App {
  retry(fn: () => void) {
    fn();
  }
  load(attempt: number) {}
}
```

`retry` calls `fn` with no arguments, so `attempt` is always `undefined`. In a `.ts` file, TypeScript rejects this call:

```text
TS2345: Argument of type '(attempt: any) => void' is not assignable to parameter of type '() => void'.
  Target signature provides too few arguments. Expected 1 or more, but got 0.
```

In the template, Angular reports nothing. The same happens when a callback returns a function instead of a value, such as `count.update((v) => () => v + 1)`.

TypeScript places most callback errors elsewhere, so Angular still reports them. For example, `count.update((v) => String(v))` reports TS2322 at `String(v)`.

Expected: Angular reports the error at the parameter (`attempt`), the same way it reports any other template type error.

**Cause:** the type-check code marks every arrow function parameter with a "skip diagnostics" comment ([expression.ts#L386](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler/src/typecheck/expression.ts#L386)), so [`findSourceLocation`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/tcb_util.ts#L211) drops every error that starts there. The marker was meant to hide implicit `any` errors on parameters that templates can't annotate, but [`shouldReportDiagnostic`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/diagnostics.ts#L29) already filters those by error code.

**Fix:** the linked PR gives each parameter its source location instead of the marker. Inferred parameter types don't change. Implicit `any` and unused-parameter errors stay hidden.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No hosted reproduction. The snippet in the description is self-contained: paste it into any Angular 21.2+ app with `strictTemplates` turned on. The linked PR adds regression tests.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
None. The template compiles without errors.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 21.2.0 and later, including 22.2.x and 22.3.0-next.2 (main at 5d929e57e4).
Reproduced with compiler-cli tests in packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc/template_typecheck_spec.ts.
```

### Anything else?

Template arrow functions were added in 21.2.0, and the marker has been there since.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): detect @angular/core compilations like ngtsc in the preprocessor
Issues.Body:
The preprocessor recognized `@angular/core` by walking up to the nearest `package.json` named `@angular/core`, which ngtsc never does and which a host without file system access cannot do. Follow ngtsc's rule instead: the internal `angularCoreCompilation` option, falling back to the tsconfig's `_isAngularCoreCompilation`, then to an explicit `r3SymbolsFile`, and otherwise to whether the root `r3_symbols.ts` exports `ITS_JUST_ANGULAR = true` (ngtsc's `isAngularCorePackage`).

The `ITS_JUST_ANGULAR` check reads `r3_symbols.ts` through the query engine, so edits to it invalidate dependent analyses. A new pseudo-dependency on the `r3_symbols.ts` root lookup re-runs only the queries that read it when the roots add or remove that file, instead of every query on each root change.

Also remove the unused `resolve_to_dts` helper.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): detect @angular/core compilations like ngtsc in the preprocessor" (#71731)

Issues.Title: fix(platform-browser): remove test root elements whose id was replaced by a host binding
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`DOMTestComponentRenderer` removes the root elements of earlier tests with `querySelectorAll('[id^=root]')`. When the root component sets or removes its own `id` (`host: {'[attr.id]': ...}`, `[id]`, `@HostBinding('attr.id')`), the `root<N>` id is gone, so the element is never removed. It stays in `document.body` for the rest of the run, and every later test that creates the component adds another one.

Issue Number: #35215

## What is the new behavior?

The renderer also keeps a reference to the root element it inserted last and removes it at the same points as the elements matched by id (module teardown, and the next `insertRootElement`). One reference is enough because `insertRootElement` already removes the previous root elements before it adds a new one.

The `root<N>` id and the `#root<N>` selector that TestBed passes to `ComponentFactory.create` are unchanged, so custom `TestComponentRenderer` implementations are not affected. Changing that selector is what held back #59711 (failures with custom renderers, per the comments there). Those custom renderers also keep their current behaviour for this bug.

The reference lives outside the class because every testing module gets its own renderer instance: with `destroyAfterEach: false`, the element of one test is removed by the next test's renderer.

Because the element is now removed by reference, two cases change besides the host binding one:

- it is also removed when the component removed its id, when the test moved it out of the document (for example into a detached container or a shadow root), or when a later test provides a different `DOCUMENT`;
- if a test creates a second component, the first root element is detached even when its id was replaced. Root elements that keep their id are already detached in that case today.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- New tests in `packages/core/test/test_bed_spec.ts` cover module teardown enabled and disabled.
- I could not run the Bazel targets locally. I ran the two new tests and the rest of the `TestBed module teardown` block against the published 22.2.3 packages in JIT mode with Jasmine, with the same change applied to `@angular/platform-browser/fesm2022/testing.mjs`. I used two environments with zoneless change detection: `BrowserTestingModule` with jsdom, and `ServerTestingModule` with domino as in `tools/testing/node_tests.init.mts`. Neither loads zone.js, and the browser one has no `NoopAnimationsModule`. In both, the two new tests fail without the change and pass with it, and the other tests pass in both cases.
- The same problem was reported downstream in testing-library/angular-testing-library#398.
- Not changed here: the `[id^=root]` query also removes the user's own elements whose id starts with `root` (for example `#rootMenu`) when a component is created and at module teardown. Should that be narrowed in this PR, or in a separate issue?

Fixes #35215

Issues.Title: [20.3.x] build: update cypress-io/github-action action to v7.4.6
Issues.Body:
Updates `cypress-io/github-action` from `v6.10.2` to `v7.4.6` (matching `main` in #71110 and `22.2.x` in #71112).

GitHub Actions runners now use Node.js 24.20+ (and force Node 20 actions onto Node 24), where `got@11` (used by `cypress-io/github-action` prior to `v7.4.4`) fails immediately with `ERR_SOCKET_CLOSED_BEFORE_CONNECTION` (`Socket closed before the connection was established`) when polling `wait-on: http://localhost:4200` before the devserver starts (see https://github.com/cypress-io/github-action/pull/1874). Upgrading to `v7.4.6` migrates the polling client to `got@16` and fixes the `devtools` Cypress CI failure on `20.3.x`.

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.9`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.9): pnpm 11.28.9 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.8...v11.28.9) This release fixes a crash on registry responses with too many content encodings ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)) and sizes the install worker pool by the container's CPU quota. A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on more setting changes. ##### Patch Changes ##### Crashes and security - A registry response with too many content encodings can no longer crash pnpm. pnpm now uses undici 7.30.1, which fixes [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c). - `pnpm install` now sizes its worker pool by the CPU quota of the container it runs in, such as a Kubernetes CPU limit, when that quota is smaller than the number of CPUs the container may run on. The default `workspaceConcurrency` respects the quota the same way. On a CI runner with a 4-CPU quota and hundreds of host CPUs, pnpm started hundreds of workers and ran out of memory [#​17382](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17382). ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail when the `node-linker` setting differs from the one recorded in `node_modules`. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace recreates `node_modules` with the new `node-linker`, and an install filtered to some projects fails [pnpm/tasks#203](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/203). - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer report the dependencies as out of date after a lockfile change when `dedupePeers` is `true` [#​17322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17322). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm install` now applies the `serverType` registry setting when it updates the lockfile for an override or catalog change without a full resolution. pnpm wrote the tarball URLs of a declared registry into the lockfile in that case. - Added the `pnpr` value to the `serverType` registry setting. pnpm leaves the tarball URLs of a pnpr registry out of `pnpm-lock.yaml`. - A `registries` entry whose `prefix` is `__proto__` is no longer ignored. - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). ##### Registries, proxies, and downloading pnpm - The proxy settings `httpProxy`, `httpsProxy`, `noProxy`, `proxy`, and `noproxy` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, or as `--config.httpsProxy` on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Previously, these requests read the proxy only from `.npmrc` and the `HTTPS_PROXY` family of variables [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When `https-proxy` is `false`, pnpm now downloads the pnpm version pinned by `packageManager` through the legacy `proxy` setting, as installs already do. Setting `proxy` to `false` now also stops that download from using the `HTTP_PROXY` environment variable. The signature check of the pinned pnpm now uses the same proxy and TLS settings as its download [pnpm/tasks#193](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/193). - `strictSsl` and `localAddress` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_STRICT_SSL` and `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCAL_ADDRESS`, or on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. These requests read them from `.npmrc` only before. `--config.localAddress` now reaches them in the camelCase spelling too [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). ##### Commands - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` again include the files of a `publishConfig.directory` that is reached through a symlink, together with its bundled dependencies [#​17390](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17390). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages that a project still uses when pnpm copied or cloned them into `node_modules`. These include patched packages, built packages, and every package installed with `packageImportMethod: copy`. Before, the prune removed them, and the next install downloaded them again [#​7192](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7192). - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages of a project that was installed with a different symlinked spelling of the store path. Previously, prune dropped such a project from its list and removed the packages only that project used from the global virtual store. ##### Speed and output - Sped up installs of projects whose local directory dependencies share transitive local directory dependencies. pnpm no longer checks a shared directory again for each direct dependency that reaches it [#​17374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17374). - Output that fills the terminal, such as `pnpm run --stream` script output, is now written once. Before, every new line also rewrote all the lines already on screen [#​17387](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17387). - The warning about unrecognized settings now marks `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` as a setting of a newer pnpm version. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors

The previously embedded Node.js 26.0.0 still trusted the certificate authority intermediates that Node.js distrusted in October 2026, so a standalone pnpm accepted TLS certificates issued under them. ##### Platinum Sponsors

##### 0.75.0

Additional documentation can be found at: <https://bazelbuild.github.io/rules_rust/#setup>

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust", version = "0.75.0")
```

##### Extensions

##### Bindgen

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust_bindgen", version = "0.75.0")
```

##### MdBook

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust_mdbook", version = "0.75.0")
```

##### Prost

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust_prost", version = "0.75.0")
```

##### PyO3

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust_pyo3", version = "0.75.0")
```

##### Wasm-Bindgen

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust_wasm_bindgen", version = "0.75.0")
```

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0) This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing. ##### Minor Changes - Added a repeatable global `--env-file ` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111). - pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222). - Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387). ##### Installing packages - A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack. - Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319). - pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205). - pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224). - Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install. - A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`. - `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395). - Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report: - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store. - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory. - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read. - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`. `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`. - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235). - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198). - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). - Registry revisions are now addressed at `/@+r` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208). ##### Adding packages and global packages - `pnpm add @` and `pnpm add @` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234). - `pnpm add ` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`. - `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`. - `pnpm -D install ` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install ` was rejected as an unexpected argument. - `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`. - Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store. - `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code. ##### Registries, proxies, and login - pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). - When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. - `pnpm login` saves the token in `/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting. - pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184). ##### Running scripts and other commands - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209). - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm -r run

Issues.Title: docs(service-worker): clarify how applicationMaxAge is measured
Issues.Body:
`applicationMaxAge` counts from the build time (the `timestamp` in `ngsw.json`), not from when files were cached on the device. After that age, the service worker skips the cache even if the build is still the latest, so the app stops working offline until you deploy a new one. If you omit the property, there's no limit. The guide and schema didn't say any of this, so this PR clarifies both.

Fixes #71720

Issues.Title: docs(service-worker): applicationMaxAge is counted from the build timestamp, and the default is not documented
Issues.Body:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

The `applicationMaxAge` section says it configures "how long the service worker will cache any requests", which reads as an age counted from when the files were cached on the device. In the worker, the age is actually counted from the manifest `timestamp`, which is set at build time (`timestamp: Date.now()` in the config generator):

```ts
const isVersionWithinMaxAge =
  appVersion?.manifest.applicationMaxAge === undefined ||
  this.adapter.time - appVersion.manifest.timestamp < appVersion.manifest.applicationMaxAge;
```

(`packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts`)

So once the build is older than `applicationMaxAge`, every client bypasses the cache and goes to the network, even if the cached version is still the latest one deployed. If no new version is deployed within that window, the app no longer starts offline.

The page also does not say what happens when the property is not set: from the code above, there is no limit (cached versions are served regardless of age).

### Enter the URL of the topic with the problem

https://angular.dev/ecosystem/service-workers/config#applicationmaxage

### Describe what you were looking for in the documentation

From when the max age is counted, and the default behavior when `applicationMaxAge` is omitted.

### Describe the actions that led you to experience the problem

We set `"applicationMaxAge": "1d12h"`, expecting cached files to be refreshed after 36 hours on each device. Instead, 36 hours after each build, the service worker stopped serving the app from its cache on all devices. Online this is invisible (the network answers), but offline the app does not start until a new version is built and deployed.

### Describe what you want to experience that would fix the problem

State explicitly that:
- the age is measured from the build time (manifest `timestamp`), not from when the files were cached on the device;
- beyond it, the cache is bypassed even when no newer version exists, which disables offline support until the next deployment;
- when omitted, there is no maximum age (current default behavior).

### Add a screenshot if that helps illustrate the problem

_No response_


```true

```

### Provide any additional information here in as much as detail as you can

```true
The JSON schema description ("how long the entire application is allowed to remain in the cache before being considered invalid") has the same ambiguity and could be clarified the same way.
```
